source_bindings.claim: Use the finite exponential family, minimality, convex hull, affine hull, and relative-interior definitions from the A-page finite-family Definition. Assume the representation is minimal. The sample space is $X^n$ with product mass $\prod_{i=1}^n\pi_\theta(x_i)$, which is the IID sampling model; $n\ge1$. For a realized tuple $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$, set $\bar T=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nT(x_i)$ and $K=\operatorname{conv}(T(X))$. A finite MLE is a parameter $\hat\theta\in\mathbb R^k$ attaining the maximum of that likelihood. Then a finite MLE exists if and only if $\bar T\in\operatorname{ri}K$, and when it exists it is unique.

Let $X=\{-1,+1\}$, $w(-1)=w(+1)=1$, and $T(\sigma)=\sigma$. For a finite field $h\in\mathbb R$, the Gibbs probabilities are
$$\pi_h(+1)=\frac{e^h}{e^h+e^{-h}},\qquad \pi_h(-1)=\frac{e^{-h}}{e^h+e^{-h}}.$$
For a sample of $n\ge1$ spins all equal to $+1$, the log likelihood is
$$\ell(h)=n\left(h-\log(e^h+e^{-h})\right).$$
It is strictly increasing at every finite $h$, so the likelihood has no finite maximizer. The empirical statistic mean is $1$, a boundary point of $\operatorname{conv}\{-1,+1\}=[-1,1]$.
